2030 round 2, original team MIN, previously acquired by OKC

context.SAC: Kings were 1-9, worst start in the league, yet moved a 24-year-old first-rounder who fit a rebuild. Coach cited a logjam and competition (Sharp rookie, Monk back). Trade saved about $3M in tax (Kings now about $6M under the tax line), cleared a roster spot, created a $3.3M exception, and gave the Kings their first second-round picks in 7 years. Kings had also just traded up to #29 for Alex Karaban in June 2026.
context.OKC: Contender at 8-2 with Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace badly hurt and Chet Holmgren out for significant time; lost Dort, Wiggins, Joe in the offseason. About $4.5M below the second apron. GM Presti reportedly targeted Clifford as a cheap rotation wing/rebounder.

trades.investment_notes: Kings traded San Antonio's top-16-protected 2027 first (converts to two seconds if it does not convey) to OKC on 2025 draft night to move up to #24 and take him. About 17 months later they gave him back for two second-rounders; OKC essentially got the first-round pick for him and then re-bought him cheaply. Sunk cost ignored, and the asset value fell far below what was paid.
trades.analyst_view: Analysts and fans panned Sacramento: the return was weak against what was paid, a rebuilding team buried a young wing, and the front office showed no clear plan. OKC was praised for a cheap fix for injuries, and one writer argued that Presti's interest is itself a signal to keep a player.

multi_team_rates.note: Complete per-season counts for 2015-16 through 2024-25 could NOT be obtained: Basketball-Reference pages truncate when fetched and no outlet publishes a per-season table. Null = not measured. Figures marked approx come from outlet summaries.

by_season.note: 2009-2019 averaged about 4.5 trades per season with 3+ teams (RealGM)
about 8 trades per season with 3+ teams (RealGM), roughly double the prior decade
in-season: more than a third of 25 trades (as of the report) were 3+ teams (search summary of Hoops Rumors tracker; partial season)

Deadline week (Feb 1-5 2026) per NBA.com tracker: 23 deals listed, 6 three-team (26%), 0 four-plus. Hoops Rumors lists 28 incl. minor. Jan 9 Young trade was 2-team. Offseason 2026 (ESPN tracker, about 45 deals incl. draft pick swaps): 3-team about 4 (June 22 MIN-BKN-CHI; June 23 four-team NYK-DAL-CLE-PHX pick shuffle; July 19 OKC-ATL-DAL; Aug 19 four-team CLE-DEN-LAC-WAS). NBA.com bundles linked deals as 4 to 6-team (Randle, LaMelo, Schroder, Watson, Middleton), which conflicts with ESPN's separate-trade counts; definition matters. 2025 July: Basketball-Reference shows 18 trades through Oct 17 2025 incl. 3 three-team and one 7-team deal (Jul 6 2025).

multi_team_rates.overall_share_estimate: Roughly 20-30% of deadline-week deals and perhaps 10-15% of all trades involve 3+ teams in recent years (estimate, from the partial figures above); about 4.5 per year before 2019, about 8 per year after.
typical_shapes: Salary routing: a third team with cap room or a trade exception absorbs a contract (Bulls absorbing Saric via exception in CLE-SAC-CHI) in return for seconds.
Pick sweetener for absorbing salary: the absorbing team collects second-round picks (Chicago repeatedly in Feb 2026).
Star moves with two other teams supplying pieces (Davis deal pulled in Charlotte for Tyus Jones/Branham; Ivey/Conley/Huerter three-way with Minnesota paying a swap and saving tax).
Tax-dodge chains: one team's tax saving needs a partner and a cash/exception holder (Clippers-Raptors-Nets Chris Paul).
Draft-night pick shuffles: three or four teams chain picks and future seconds (June 23 2026 NYK-DAL-CLE-PHX).
Sign-and-trade plus exception matching in restricted free agency (Watson to CLE with Strus to LAC and picks to DEN).
